note: Adapted from the original description by Silvestri (1914) (published under the name Anoplotermes concilians and later transferred to Astalotermes); the original is in Latin; the genus has no soldier, and only the female and male alates and the worker are described; measurements are in mm as in the original.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Female alate: body length with wings 10 mm, body length without wings 6 mm; head length 0.80 mm, width 0.70 mm; long diameter of the compound eye 0.24 mm; antennal length 1.56 mm; fore wing length 8.5 mm, width 2.15 mm; hind tibia 0.90 mm. Body chestnut brown, head nearly black, clypeus reddish brown, pronotum with a barely discernible cross-shaped mark, the narrower middle of the sternites dirty milky white, wings pale smoky to hazel, costa pale yellowish brown. Fontanelle small, oval, slightly paler than the surrounding frontal area; clypeus rather inflated, slightly longer than half its width; compound eyes rather small, not very projecting; ocelli small, far from the compound eyes; antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 almost twice as long as segment 3, segments 3—5 subequal in length. Pronotum about 1/4 narrower than the width of the head including the compound eyes, posterior margin slightly concave; posterior part of the meso- and metanotum gradually narrowed, posterior margin in the middle slightly wide and deeply concave, posterior corners nearly pointed. Wing surface with sparse hairs besides those on the veins, and with small tubercles bearing 3—4 rays. Male: body length with wings 9 mm, body length without wings 5.8 mm; fore wing length 8 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 3.3 mm; head length 0.69 mm, width 0.73 mm; antennal length 1.20 mm; hind tibia 0.61 mm. Body white straw-coloured, head creamy yellow, abdomen grey from the gut contents. Upper surface of the head with numerous short hairs; clypeus slightly inflated, slightly wider than half its length; antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 scarcely longer than segment 4, segment 5 slightly shorter than segment 4. Anterior lobe of the pronotum rounded. Legs hairy, similar to the preceding species.
